cleanIntro: Caesar Guerini publishes one owner's manual for its whole over/under line, and it does not name individual models: it says its over-and-unders all function and operate in essentially the same way. Every step here is that book's general procedure, stated as the book states it. The book names the Magnus nowhere, and the one model-specific section it prints — a fore-end tension screw on the Invictus action — is not carried here. The strip itself is three pieces: fore-end, barrels, receiver with stock, and no further.

steps.title: Safety on S, muzzle somewhere safe
steps.action: Push the safety to S so the letter shows completely, and point the gun in a safe direction before your hand goes near the top lever.
steps.prose: Everything after this opens the action, and the safety is the one thing on the gun that is on before the breech is.
steps.quote: Put the safety in the “S” (on) position and point the shotgun in a safe direction.
steps.cite: Caesar Guerini Use and Maintenance Manual — Over-and-Under Shotguns — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — TO UNLOAD THE GUN, PDF p.11 (printed p.19)
steps.warn: Make sure the gun is not loaded before disassembling and cleaning it so that it will not fire accidentally.

steps.title: Top lever right, barrels down, shells out by hand
steps.action: Push the top lever to the right, hold the receiver in your shooting hand, put the other hand palm down on top of the barrels at the front of the fore-end, and push down. The breech breaks open on the hinge pin and the extractors lift the shells slightly so you can take them out by hand.
steps.prose: Live shells are not kicked out — the ejectors only throw fired hulls — so a shell you do not pull stays sitting on the extractor.
steps.quote: Push the top lever to the right, support the receiver with the shooting hand and with the other hand grasp the top of the barrels palm down at the front of the fore-end and push down.
steps.cite: Caesar Guerini Use and Maintenance Manual — Over-and-Under Shotguns — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — TO UNLOAD THE GUN, PDF p.11 (printed p.19)

steps.title: Prove both barrels empty before the strip starts
steps.action: With the action open, look into both chambers and confirm the gun is on safe with nothing in either barrel. Guerini makes this the first line of the disassembly and tells you not to skip it.
steps.prose: Two barrels means two chambers to check. One look at the bottom chamber is how a shell in the top one gets missed.
steps.quote: Make certain the shotgun is on safe and the action open with shells removed from both barrels.
steps.cite: Caesar Guerini Use and Maintenance Manual — Over-and-Under Shotguns — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — DISASSEMBLY INSTRUCTIONS, PDF p.12 (printed p.20)

steps.title: Breech closed and locked again
steps.action: Close the breech and check that the top lever has snapped back and engaged the barrels. The fore-end comes off a closed gun, not an open one.
steps.prose: With the breech closed the barrels are held by the locking bolt while the fore-end comes off; an open gun with no fore-end has nothing holding its barrels on.
steps.quote: Close the breech and make sure the top lever engages the barrels.
steps.cite: Caesar Guerini Use and Maintenance Manual — Over-and-Under Shotguns — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — DISASSEMBLY INSTRUCTIONS, PDF p.12 (printed p.20)

steps.title: Fore-end latch down, fore-end off
steps.action: Press down on the fore-end latch and take the fore-end off the barrels.
steps.prose: The fore-end is what keeps the barrels on the receiver once the breech opens. From here on, support the barrels yourself.
steps.quote: Press down on the fore-end latch and remove the fore-end
steps.cite: Caesar Guerini Use and Maintenance Manual — Over-and-Under Shotguns — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — DISASSEMBLY INSTRUCTIONS, PDF p.12 (printed p.20)

steps.title: Action open, barrels lifted off the receiver
steps.action: Open the action with the top lever, keeping hold of the barrels, and lift them off the receiver. That is the strip: fore-end, barrels, and receiver with stock. Guerini's disassembly goes no further.
steps.prose: With the fore-end off, nothing but your hand holds the barrels once the breech opens. Keep control of them so the monoblock does not drop onto the receiver face.
steps.quote: Open the action using the top lever, being careful to keep control of the barrels and carefully remove the barrels from the receiver
steps.cite: Caesar Guerini Use and Maintenance Manual — Over-and-Under Shotguns — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — DISASSEMBLY INSTRUCTIONS, PDF p.12 (printed p.20)

steps.title: Solvent patch through each bore, from the chamber end
steps.action: Wet a patch with bore solvent and push it through each bore from the chamber end. Leave it to soak while you work on the receiver.
steps.prose: Chamber end in means the fouling goes out the muzzle, not back toward the action.
steps.quote: Wet a patch with bore cleaning solvent and wet the inside of each bore by pushing the wet patch through from the chamber end of the barrel.
steps.cite: Caesar Guerini Use and Maintenance Manual — Over-and-Under Shotguns — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — BARREL SET, PDF p.12 (printed p.20)

steps.title: Brush full strokes, then patches until one comes out clean
steps.action: Change to a brush and run it from the chamber end, full strokes end to end, never reversing while the brush is still in the barrel. Then go back to patches from the rear until one comes out clean, and finish with a patch lightly wet with lubricant or preservative.
steps.prose: Reversing a brush inside the bore is what the full-stroke rule exists to stop. The last patch should leave a thin film — the bores are chrome-lined, but shot-shell residue can still corrode them if they are left bare.
steps.quote: Brush 5 to 10 full cycles (1 cycle = one stroke in and one stroke out).
steps.cite: Caesar Guerini Use and Maintenance Manual — Over-and-Under Shotguns — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — BARREL SET, PDF p.12 (printed p.20)

steps.title: Outside of the barrels wiped and covered with preservative
steps.action: Wipe the outside of both barrels clear of moisture, dirt and carbon, then cover the metal with a good preservative. Wipe off fingerprints as you go.
steps.prose: Bluing is not rust protection, and the acid in a fingerprint is enough to start rust on it.
steps.quote: Carefully wipe the outside of the barrels to remove any moisture, dirt, carbon or other residues from the bluing.
steps.cite: Caesar Guerini Use and Maintenance Manual — Over-and-Under Shotguns — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — BARREL SET, PDF p.12 (printed p.21)
steps.warn: Rust can and will occur if this step is neglected and this is NOT covered by warranty.

steps.title: A light coat of grease on the choke tube walls
steps.action: With a choke tube out, put a light coat of protective grease around its outside before it goes back in.
steps.prose: Gas gets behind the tube when the gun fires. Without the grease the outside of the tube corrodes and it can stick in the barrel.
steps.quote: we recommend covering the external circumference of the choke tube with a light quantity of protective grease.
steps.cite: Caesar Guerini Use and Maintenance Manual — Over-and-Under Shotguns — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — INSTALLATION AND REMOVAL OF CHOKE TUBES, PDF p.11 (printed p.18)

steps.title: Receiver brushed, solvent kept off the wood
steps.action: Brush residue, carbon and dirt off the receiver with a soft bristle brush and general-purpose solvent. Keep the solvent off the stock and fore-end and do not let it run down inside the receiver. Let it air dry, or blow it dry with care.
steps.prose: Solvent that runs into the receiver or soaks into the wood does more harm than the dirt it was meant to lift.
steps.quote: The receiver should have any residue/carbon/ dirt removed with a soft bristle brush and general purpose solvent.
steps.cite: Caesar Guerini Use and Maintenance Manual — Over-and-Under Shotguns — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — STOCK, RECEIVER AND FORE-END GROUP, PDF p.12 (printed p.21)

steps.title: Wood cleaned with a damp cloth, then linseed oil
steps.action: Clean dirt off the stock and fore-end with a cloth that is damp but not wet. Then rub in a small amount of boiled linseed oil, vigorously, until no excess is left on the wood.
steps.prose: Oil over dirt seals the dirt in. Oil left standing on the stock means too much was used or it was not rubbed long enough.
steps.quote: After the stock on the shotgun is cleaned it can be rubbed with boiled linseed oil
steps.cite: Caesar Guerini Use and Maintenance Manual — Over-and-Under Shotguns — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — STOCK, RECEIVER AND FORE-END GROUP, PDF p.12 (printed p.21)

steps.title: Thin film on the barrels, extra at the pivots, the fore-end latch points
steps.action: Give the barrels a thin film over the whole group. Oil the inside of the receiver lightly, with extra at the points where the barrels pivot. Lubricate the latch mechanism inside the fore-end at its specific points.
steps.prose: Guerini's "extra lubricant" means extra attention, not oil dripping off the gun.
steps.quote: Lubricate only with a thin film over the entire group (enough to prevent rust).
steps.cite: Caesar Guerini Use and Maintenance Manual — Over-and-Under Shotguns — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — LUBRICATION INSTRUCTIONS, PDF p.12 (printed p.21)

deepAbsentReason: The book ends at the field strip. Its DISASSEMBLY INSTRUCTIONS (PDF p.12, printed p.20) take the gun down to fore-end, barrels and receiver with stock and stop there; the rest of its maintenance pages are cleaning, lubrication, reassembly and adjustments (the DTS rib and stock comb, and the Invictus-only fore-end tension screw). It publishes no trigger group, ejector, firing pin or stock-removal procedure, so nothing deeper is invented here.

cleaning.name: BARREL SET
tasks: Solvent patch through each bore from the chamber end, left to soak
Bore brush from the chamber end, 5 to 10 full cycles, no reversing mid-bore
Patches from the rear until one comes out clean
A patch lightly wet with lubricant or preservative through each bore
Outside of the barrels wiped and covered with preservative

cleaning.name: CHOKE TUBES
tasks: A light coat of protective grease on the outside of each choke tube
Thread-cleaning tool on the choke key turned clockwise only

cleaning.name: RECEIVER, STOCK & FORE-END
tasks: Receiver brushed with a soft bristle brush and general-purpose solvent
Do not let solvent run onto the wood or down into the receiver
Stock and fore-end wiped with a damp, not wet, cloth
Boiled linseed oil rubbed in, no excess left

cleaning.name: LUBRICATION
tasks: Thin film over the whole barrel group
Extra at the barrel pivot points and on the extractors
Inside of the receiver lightly, extra where the barrels pivot
The latch points inside the fore-end

reassembly: Set the barrels' locking blocks on the inside of the receiver, make sure they are engaged, then move the top lever to the right and close the breech.
⚠ The gun looks assembled now but is not: if the breech is opened before the fore-end is on, the barrels will come off the receiver.
Put the fore-end on the front of the receiver and push its front toward the barrels until the fore-end catch button snaps in. Only then are the barrels safe to open.
fncheck: With the gun empty and the fore-end on, open the breech with the top lever and close it again: the barrels should stay on the receiver and the top lever should snap back to the left, locking the breech. Guerini's reassembly ends at the point where, in its words, the fore-end is secured and the barrels safe to open.
